Field evidence record

This chapter preserves the sequence of observations. Earlier unknowns or hypotheses may be superseded by later entries. Read the current system record and evidence conventions first.

08 — Photo catalog

First-floor Living Area thermostat terminal colors

Google-branded thermostat base: Y yellow, C blue, W white, G green, R red, */OB brown. Homeowner confirmed this is the first-floor Living Room / Living Area thermostat, correcting the earlier second-floor reference. Google Home screenshot confirms */OB is configured as Heat 2. Remote conductor endpoints remain unverified.

11 locally available image files are preserved in photos/ without re-encoding. Captions describe visible subjects; detailed wire interpretation is in other notes. Images below are embedded with relative Markdown links.

Session photo references

  • Photo 1.jpg shows the Yellow Room valve cover and its Honeywell V8043E1061 nameplate, including the red end-switch and yellow motor lead diagram. See valve wiring.
  • 55573.jpg shows the attic AM30 circulator nameplate, Taco 006-B4-11. See cartridge identification.

These filenames refer to chat attachments.

Mechanical room overview

View from the entrance. Both Polaris tanks are centered, the basement Lennox AM30 (AHU-1) is on the left, and the controls cabinet is on the right. The downstairs circulators are behind the tanks and out of view. Use this image to orient the plumbing survey. Supply and return paths still need to be traced.

The homeowner identifies the Caleffi mixer above the right Polaris tank as the domestic hot-water tempering valve. The domestic and space-heating circuits share the same water. The passive domestic recirculation return drops between the tanks, wraps around the right tank, and enters its lower Cold Inlet on the far side. The equivalent port on the left tank receives street cold water. The mixer receives hot water from the top of the right tank and street cold water at the opposite port. The mixed outlet opposite the adjustment handle starts the domestic recirculation loop.

Behind the Polaris tanks

The homeowner identifies the lower-left Taco as the basement radiant circulator and the adjacent Caleffi as its mechanical mixing valve. The red Grundfos above and to the right circulates the main loop upstairs and back. It corresponds to the pump drawn above the Polaris tanks on the original proposed piping diagram. Of the two light-brown Taco pumps higher in the photo, MC-1 Mix 1 is on the left and Var 1 is on the right. Both pumps flow right to left in this view.

Three first-floor Honeywell zone valves sit in a row, front to back in this view. Their order is Master Bath, Master Bedroom, then Main (Living Area). The nearest valve, labeled Master Bath, is visible. Two expansion tanks are visible at lower right. The red Grundfos flows left to right in this view. The loop goes to the attic AM30 first, then to the Var 2 and Mix 2 assembly. At the right edge, the nearer riser is the supply from the Grundfos. Behind it, the partly obscured return drops vertically, crosses past the two expansion-tank connections, and continues to the Polaris return.

Attic mechanical room overview

The attic Lennox AM30 (AHU-2) is on the right and the hydronic piping is on the left. The homeowner identifies the black foam-insulated pipes crossing toward the unit as the AM30 coil piping. The unit houses the Taco 006-B4-11 circulator under separate investigation. Supply and return identification in this view is pending.

Attic plumbing wall

The two upstairs Honeywell motorized valves are visible high on the wall above the Honeywell MiniZone panel. The homeowner identifies these as the valves tested for the Yellow Room and Rest of Second Floor. The left valve serves Rest of Second Floor and the right valve serves Yellow Room. The Rest of Second Floor supply continues left through its valve. The Yellow Room supply turns back to the right before reaching its valve. The homeowner suspects a direct connection between the wall thermostat and MiniZone. The panel model, terminal assignments and cable routing remain to be verified.

In this view, the main-loop return is on the left and the main-loop supply is on the right. The homeowner traced both pipes straight down through the framed wall’s bottom plate, below the visible area.

Attic plumbing wall, right-hand view

This overlaps the prior plumbing-wall photo at the Honeywell valve in the upper left. The switch labeled “Furnace” supplies power to the attic Lennox AM30 air handler (AHU-2). The homeowner reports that the high-point air eliminator beside the valve is in service.

The brown Taco on the radiant supply is Mix 2. The Taco on the right above the red and green valve handles is Var 2. The pipes projecting toward the camera serve the AM30 coil. See the attic pipe routing.

Mix 2 circulator nameplate

The nameplate identifies Mix 2 as Taco 008-BC6, rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.84 A and 1/25 hp. The homeowner confirmed that flow is right to left in the right-hand attic plumbing-wall view.

Var 2 injection circulator

The homeowner confirmed upward flow through the vertical Var 2 run. The Taco nameplate appears to read 008-BC6. Flash glare makes the model reading provisional.

Yellow Room radiant manifold

The homeowner identifies this manifold at the far end of the attic mechanical room. Var 2 is partly visible at the left edge and is the rightmost pump in the earlier right-hand plumbing-wall view. Insulated loop pipes descend from the manifold. In this view, the right header with the small valves supplies the floor loops and the left header collects their return.

Rest of Second Floor radiant manifold

In this view, the lower header farther from the camera supplies the floor loops and has the small valves. The upper header closer to the camera collects the return.

SUP 2 sensor at Mix 2

View from above Mix 2, with flow from the background toward the camera. The blue leads with the tekmar 071 tag enter the black pipe insulation immediately upstream of the pump inlet. The sensor body is concealed by the insulation. The pump wiring cover was off for this photo.

Attic MiniZone panel interior

See the terminal and cable observations.

Polaris heating outlet branches

The right Polaris heating outlet feeds two tees and an elbow. From the tank, these feed basement radiant, the red Grundfos, and the basement AM30, respectively. The Grundfos is visible in the background. The green-handled valve identifies the basement AM30 return, which joins the common heating return near the Polaris.

Polaris intertank heating pipe

The insulated pipe nearest the camera leaves the upper Heating System Outlet of the foreground Polaris (left in the entrance view). It bends across the tanks and drops to the lower Heating System Inlet of the second Polaris (right in the entrance view).

Mix 1 and Var 1 piping

Mix 1 is on the left and Var 1 is on the right. Both pumps flow right to left in this view. The two closely spaced tees at right connect the first-floor radiant circuit to the main return from upstairs. A blue sensor lead is visible just right of Mix 1. Its terminal assignment remains to be verified. The common first-floor return manifold is visible just below Mix 1. It collects the returns from Master Bath, Master Bedroom, and Main (Living Area). The lower pipe beneath Var 1 carries water back to the main return. The upper branch through Var 1 draws from that main return and injects toward Mix 1.

Mix 1 zone valves and manifolds

Overhead view of the crowded first-floor valve and manifold assembly behind the Polaris tanks. The Honeywell valve heads are on the left, with Master Bath nearest the camera. A copper supply header with three valved loop connections is visible on the right. Elbows turn the flow left to right in this view, from the valves toward the supply manifolds.

Basement radiant mixer and circulator

The Caleffi mixer is at upper right, with the incoming hot supply above it. The Taco circulator in the foreground discharges directly into the basement radiant supply manifold. The front and rear pipes behind the wiring at right are separate at the apparent tee. The mixer bottom port runs down and across to the basement return manifold, which continues to the common return tee by the expansion tanks.

Domestic Caleffi mixer from above

The exposed copper pipe in the foreground runs from the top hot outlet of the right Polaris to the domestic Caleffi mixer (TMV-2). The opposite port receives street cold water. The mixed outlet feeds the domestic distribution and passive recirculation loop. A dial thermometer is visible near the valve. The homeowner confirmed from the SupplyHouse receipt that TMV-2 is a Caleffi 521 MixCal, SKU 521519AC, a 3/4-inch sweat three-way thermostatic mixing valve with temperature gauge and check valve.

Left Polaris nameplate

American Water Heater Company Polaris PG10 34-150-2NV, serial 0448117372, product 0320092. Natural gas, 150,000 BTU/hr input, 34 US gallons, direct vent. The nameplate specifies operation at a water outlet temperature of 160 °F. The reported setting of approximately 170 °F applies to the right tank.

Right Polaris nameplate

Polaris PG10 34-150-2NV, serial 0449124485, product 0320092. The visible plate identifies natural gas and direct vent installation and shows a 160 °F water outlet temperature marking. A pipe obscures part of the ratings panel.

Grundfos main-loop circulator

The nameplate reads UPS 26-99 BFC, P/N 52722518 P1, and PC 1240. It lists 115 V, 60 Hz, single phase, three speeds, and a check valve. Grundfos lists product number 52722518 for this model. Its production code format indicates week 40 of 2012. Grundfos model cross-reference · Grundfos production code guide

Blue tape reads “Boiler Enable From Wirsbo.” This is a field label. The homeowner later traced incoming black hot to MC-1 terminal 6 and terminal 5 to the pump hot. The white pump conductor returns to supply neutral.

Basement Lennox cooling coil and pressure documentation

The basement Lennox C26-41-1, serial 6099H46722, is the refrigerant evaporator coil. Its plate lists HCFC-22 and 450 psi maximum design pressure on the refrigerant side. See the separate AM30 cabinet nameplate.

The Lennox dealer/installer letter dated October 1, 1999 describes a CompleteHeat installation requirement for an external 3/4-inch water pressure-reducing valve and thermal expansion tank. It cites unregulated supply pressure above 55 psi and large fluctuations as concerns. This is historical product documentation. The presence and location of a pressure-reducing valve in the current Polaris piping remain unverified.

The basement instrument is a combination temperature and pressure gauge. The photo shows approximately 90 °F and 65 psi on the inner blue pressure scale. The homeowner identifies its location as the Mix 1 discharge before the three main-floor zone valves. Operating conditions and gauge accuracy remain unverified.

Basement AM30 cabinet nameplate

Lennox AM30Q2/3-70-2, serial 5898M07675. The plate lists 120 V, 60 Hz, single phase, a 1/40 hp water pump rated 0.52 A, and a maximum water inlet temperature of 180 °F. It specifies potable-water-compatible piping and fittings and prohibits adding boiler treatment chemicals.

Basement AM30 wiring diagram

The cabinet door carries the Lennox AM30-2 Series factory wiring diagram, form 532,890W, dated 6/98. It shows the thermostat terminal block, blower speed taps, water-pump circuits, freeze-stat, and HM30 interface. Field wiring and optional components require separate verification.

Basement AM30 circulator nameplate

The internal AHU-1 circulator is a Taco 006-B4-11, rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp. The attic AHU-2 has a separate pump of the same model.

Attic AM30 and circulator nameplates

AHU-2 is Lennox AM30Q2-40-2, serial 5801K48409. The cabinet plate lists a maximum water inlet temperature of 180 °F. The internal circulator is Taco 006-B4-11, rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp.

Basement radiant circulator nameplate

The dedicated basement radiant circulator is a Taco 006-B4-11, rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp. Both AM30 internal circulators also use this model.

Mix 1 circulator nameplate

Mix 1 is a Taco 006-B4-11, rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp. The nameplate faces the wall and a manifold hose partly blocks it, making it unreadable from the usual service position. This close-up captures the identifying details.

Var 1 circulator nameplate

Var 1 is a Taco 008-BC6, rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.84 A and 1/25 hp.

DuoMix 201 terminal strip

Straight-on view of MC-1 showing the demand, line-voltage and sensor terminals. The sensor strip spans terminals 17–27. A blue lead is visible at 20 Sup2 and a red lead at 23 Sup1. The faceplate marks the sensor strip “Do not apply power.” See the terminal reference.

Common heating return temperature probe

The blue leads behind the Grundfos enter insulation on the common heating return. The probe is left of the expansion tanks and downstream of the basement radiant return tee, toward the left Polaris. It is the likely MC-1 BRet sensor. The cable termination has yet to be traced.

Basement MABS EZ-4 panel

The Trol-A-Temp MABS EZ-4 is mounted below the DuoMix. The cover diagram documents factory terminal functions. The installed board is labeled Living Room, Master Bedroom and Basement for Zones 1–3. See the controls reference.

Basement AM30 low-voltage wiring

The close-up shows the five-screw TB1 block and multiple field conductors. The wider view places it at the bottom of the control board, below the pump wiring. See the factory diagram and field observations.

Duct dampers reference photo

The photo shows damper actuators on duct branches. Retained for reference. The current survey covers plumbing and main system controls through the Lennox AM30 units.

ZCM boards, relays and zone tags

This cabinet view shows two black relay assemblies above ZCM-1 and three between the boards, above ZCM-2. Visible cable tags include Living Area, Master Bedroom, Master Bath, and Bedroom Above Garage. ZCM-1 is marked A303XX0003. The relay model and pinout are unreadable from this angle.

Upper ZCM relay nameplates

Above ZCM-1, the right relay is MARS 90293 (label also shows D4600), and the left relay is White-Rodgers 90-293Q. Both labels specify a 24 VAC, 50/60 Hz coil. The nearby zone tags label cables. Relay assignments require a wiring trace.

Lower-right relay above ZCM-2

The side label shows White-Rodgers, a 24 V 50/60 Hz coil, and a printed switching diagram. Wiring obscures the exact model number. The nearby SPARE tag identifies a cable. Its relationship to this relay remains unverified.

Cabinet Honeywell switching relay

Front view of the brown Honeywell R8222D1014 beside MC-1. Its 24 VAC coil shares a transformer conductor with the two upper black relays. The switched black lead feeds the basement radiant Taco.
